label: Mid original-phase steps (t=3-6) of sequences starting with n, peaking on n ? j d prefixes
explanation: Sparse prefix-conjunction feature. Fires only during the original phase at steps 3-6 (61% of mass at t=4), plus a small tail at the delimiter; never during copy. About 69% of mass comes from sequences whose first token is n (19x lift). The strongest activations are on n-initial prefixes with j at position 1 or 2 and d at position 3 (e.g. n j 3 d [y], n j j d [i]); the step right after d is strongest (prev_tok d lift 13x, prev2_tok j lift 8x). Other prefixes with similar tokens (j, d, 3, k, p after g/z/o starts) give weak activations. Activation magnitude rises with how closely the prefix matches n_jd. The simple predicate (n-initial, t 3-6) has high mass recall but very low precision (~5%): most n-initial sequences do not trigger it. The exact token conjunction that is required could not be captured with a compact predicate. Does not fire at t<3, at t>6, or anywhere in the copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+8.03), prev_tok=d (+5.52), orig0=g (+4.38), orig0=z (+3.93), phase=0 & in_tok=y (+3.45), orig1=j (+3.31). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-3.95), orig_idx=-1 (-3.38), orig1=d (-3.30), orig1=0 (-3.16).
